title: GCAM as research software
summary: Treat GCAM as research software: know the pipeline from source data to results, how the solver works, what calibration fixes, and what you must keep to rebuild any run.
outcomes: Trace a GCAM run from gcamdata and input XML through the solver to the output database and queries
Explain why GCAM solves for market-clearing prices period by period rather than optimising over time
Say what share-weights do in calibration and why they are not free parameters
List the four things you must archive to rebuild a run: version, inputs, configuration and queries
narration_en: Research with GCAM starts with knowing exactly what you are running. GCAM is a pipeline. Source data are processed by an R package called gcamdata into XML input files. A configuration file lists which input files to load, in which order, and the solver settings. The core model then solves one period at a time: it searches for the prices that make supply equal demand in every market, then moves five years on. It does not look ahead. Results go into a database, and you pull them out with queries, in R with rgcam or in Python with gcamreader. In the base year, share-weights are calibrated so that the model reproduces observed data; after that they are assumptions you choose and must report. One warning before anything else: the latest release is version 9.1, but the online documentation describes version 8.2, and transport units changed in between. Always write down the version, the input files, the configuration and the queries, so that anyone can rebuild your results.
narration_ar: يبدأ البحث باستخدام نموذج GCAM بمعرفة ما تشغّله بالضبط. فالنموذج سلسلة من الخطوات المتتابعة: تُعالَج البيانات المصدرية بحزمة R تُسمّى gcamdata لتتحول إلى ملفات إدخال بصيغة XML. ويحدد ملف الإعدادات ملفات الإدخال التي تُحمَّل وترتيب تحميلها وإعدادات أداة الحل. ثم يحل النموذج فترةً زمنية واحدة في كل مرة: يبحث عن الأسعار التي تجعل العرض مساويًا للطلب في كل الأسواق، ثم ينتقل خمس سنوات إلى الأمام، دون أن ينظر إلى المستقبل. وتُحفَظ النتائج في قاعدة بيانات تُستخرج منها بالاستعلامات، في لغة R عبر rgcam أو في Python عبر gcamreader. وفي سنة الأساس تُعايَر أوزان الحصص لكي يعيد النموذج إنتاج البيانات المرصودة، وبعد ذلك تصبح افتراضات تختارها أنت ويجب أن تذكرها. وتنبيه قبل كل شيء: أحدث إصدار هو 9.1، لكن التوثيق المنشور على الإنترنت يصف الإصدار 8.2، وقد تغيّرت وحدات النقل بينهما. لذلك دوِّن دائمًا رقم الإصدار وملفات الإدخال وملف الإعدادات والاستعلامات، حتى يتمكن أي شخص من إعادة بناء نتائجك.

diagram.title: The GCAM pipeline, from data to findings
diagram.caption: Every result you publish sits at the end of this chain; each link is something you must record.

nodes.label: Source data
nodes.detail: Raw statistics and assumptions: energy balances, land and crop data, transport costs and intensities, population and GDP pathways.

nodes.label: gcamdata
nodes.detail: R code that turns source data into GCAM's input XML files, chunk by chunk. Systematic changes to assumptions belong here.

nodes.label: Input XML
nodes.detail: The files GCAM actually reads, such as transportation_UCD_CORE.xml. Since v8.5 transport uses billion pkm and 1975 dollars.

nodes.label: Your add-on XML
nodes.detail: Small files that change selected inputs: a lower BEV cost, a new share-weight path, a carbon tax. Later files override earlier ones.

nodes.label: Configuration
nodes.detail: configuration.xml lists the ScenarioComponents in load order, the scenario name, the output database and the solver configuration.

nodes.label: GCAM core
nodes.detail: C++ model: in each 5-year period the solver adjusts prices until every market clears, then moves on. No foresight.

nodes.label: Output database
nodes.detail: Results are written to a BaseX XML database such as database_basexdb.

nodes.label: Queries
nodes.detail: Saved queries pull tables out of the database into R (rgcam) or Python (gcamreader).

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.detail: Tidy tables, differences from Reference, decompositions and figures: scripted, versioned and rerunnable.

tour.text: Source data become input XML through gcamdata. To change an assumption everywhere, change it here and rebuild.
For a scenario, add a small XML file and list it in the configuration after the base files. Later files override earlier ones.
GCAM reads the configuration and solves each 5-year period for prices that clear every market.
Results go to a database; queries pull out exactly the tables you need.
Your analysis scripts turn query tables into findings. Keep them under version control with everything upstream.

sections.heading: The pipeline in one picture
sections.html:
GCAM is not one program but a chain of tools. Raw data (IEA energy balances, the UC Davis transport database, FAO land data, SSP population and GDP) is processed by gcamdata, an R package, into hundreds of input XML files. A configuration file lists which XML files to read and in what order. The C++ core reads them, solves every market in every period, and writes results to a BaseX output database. You read the database with queries, from ModelInterface, R (rgcam) or Python (gcamreader).

Five facts to settle before any study

sections.heading: How GCAM solves: markets, not optimisation
sections.html:
Every period, GCAM looks for a set of prices at which supply equals demand in every market at once: crude oil, electricity in each region, land in each land unit, water in each basin, and constraint markets such as a CO2 cap. Write the excess demand of market m as a function of all prices p:

Fm(p) = Dm(p) − Sm(p) = 0    for every market m(3.1)

The solver works in log prices and scales each market's excess demand so that a market measured in EJ and one measured in km³ count equally. Its main engine is Broyden's method: a Newton-like step that reuses an approximate Jacobian instead of recomputing all derivatives each iteration. Bisection and a preconditioner bring starting guesses close enough for Broyden to converge. A typical regional run solves a few hundred markets.

Bk δx = −F(xk),   x = ln p,   then B is updated from the observed change in F(3.2)

The model is recursive-dynamic: each period is solved with the information of that period only, then the model steps forward five years. Nobody in GCAM knows a carbon price is coming; plants built in 2030 stay until they retire even if a policy arrives in 2035. This is the main contrast with intertemporal optimisation models such as MESSAGEix (Go 2, module 2.8).

Was the run solved? Read the log

A finished GCAM run is not the same as a solved one. Each period's solution is written to exe/logs/main_log.txt; a run that completes ends with "Model exiting successfully". If a period fails to reach the tolerance within max-model-calcs, the solver reports it and the model continues from an unsolved state. Results from an unsolved period look like any other numbers in the database.

Solver setting (example configuration)ValueMeaning
solution-tolerance0.001relative excess demand accepted as "cleared"
solution-floor0.0001absolute floor for tiny markets
calibration-tolerance0.01how close base-year outputs must be to data
max-model-calcs2500budget of model evaluations per period
Broyden ftol / max-iterations1e-3 / 25rule: solution-tolerance ≥ Broyden ftol

Values from the sample solver configuration in the documentation's solver page; the compiled defaults are not given there.

sections.heading: Calibration: what the share-weights are doing
sections.html: In every base year GCAM must reproduce observed energy use by fuel, sector and region. It does this by solving for share-weights: the αi in the logit share equation (module 3.2). Whatever the costs say, the share-weight adjusts so that the base-year shares match the data. In the future, the share-weights are carried forward or moved along assumed paths (interpolation rules). This is powerful and dangerous: a share-weight silently absorbs everything the cost data miss, including infrastructure, preferences, regulation and data error.

callouts.title: Why this matters
callouts.html: GCAM v9.1 was released on 2 June 2026, but its online documentation still describes v8.2. Between the two, the transport input files changed their units from million to billion passenger-km and from 1990 to 1975 dollars. A number copied from a v8.2 tutorial into a v9.1 add-on file can be wrong by a factor of 1,000, and GCAM will still run. Research with GCAM starts with knowing exactly which version, which file and which unit you are touching.

callouts.title: In GCAM
callouts.html: Region list: input/gcamdata/inst/extdata/common/GCAM_region_names.csv (32 rows in v9.1). Final calibration year: MODEL_BASE_YEARS in input/gcamdata/R/constants.R. Release notes: updates.html in the documentation and the GitHub release page. Saudi Arabia → "Middle East" for transport parameters in energy/mappings/UCD_ctry.csv.

callouts.title: Worked calculation
callouts.html:
One market, by hand, the way Broyden would

  1. Excess demand F(p) = 1000 − 4p − 6p. Guess p0 = 80: F = 1000 − 800 = 200.
  2. Second guess p1 = 90: F = 1000 − 900 = 100.
  3. Secant slope B = (100 − 200) ÷ (90 − 80) = −10.
  4. Step δp = −F ÷ B = −100 ÷ −10 = 10, so p2 = 100.
  5. F(100) = 1000 − 1000 = 0: solved. In one dimension Broyden is the secant method; in many dimensions it updates a whole matrix of such slopes.

Answer: price 100, as in the week 4 toy market

callouts.title: Pitfall
callouts.html: "The run finished, so the scenario is valid." Unsolved periods, a constraint that is not binding (and so cannot be solved as a market), or an add-on file silently ignored because of a misspelt region name all produce a database. Every research run needs three checks: the log says each period solved; the base years reproduce calibration data; the variable you changed actually changed in the output (query it directly).

callouts.title: Research note
callouts.html: Treat future share-weight paths as assumptions you must report, not as model output. In the current transport files, battery-electric car share-weights are 0 until the first future year and reach 1 by 2030 along an s-curve; in v5.4 they were 0.25 in 2030 and 0.625 in 2050 (A54.globaltranTech_shrwt_revised.csv). The same costs give very different electric-vehicle futures under the two paths. Module 3.6 shows how to test this.

callouts.title: Try it
callouts.html:
1. Open exe/configuration_ref.xml in your release and find the line that loads the transport file. Which file is it, and what comes immediately after it? (Answer key.)
  2. Explain in two sentences why an add-on file must be listed after transportation_UCD_CORE.xml.

takeaways: A GCAM result is the end of a chain: source data, gcamdata, input XML, configuration, solver, database, queries
GCAM is recursive-dynamic: it clears markets one 5-year period at a time, with no foresight
Share-weights reproduce the base year; after that they are your assumptions and must be reported
Record version, inputs, configuration and queries; the docs describe v8.2 while the release is 9.1

quiz.q: What does GCAM solve for in each period?
options: Prices that clear every market at once
quiz.explain: GCAM is a partial-equilibrium model that searches for market-clearing prices in each period.

quiz.q: Two add-on files change the same input. Which value does GCAM use?
options: The file listed later in the configuration
quiz.explain: Files are read in order, so a later file overrides an earlier one.

quiz.q: In the base year, share-weights are…
quiz.explain: Calibration finds share-weights that reproduce base-year shares at base-year costs.

quiz.q: Why can a number copied from an older tutorial be wrong by a factor of 1,000?
options: Transport units changed from million to billion pkm in v8.5
quiz.explain: Version 8.5 changed transport units (and the price base year); always check units against your release.

glossary.def: The R package that builds GCAM's input XML files from source data.
A small XML input file that changes selected values and is loaded after the base files.
Solving one period at a time, using only information up to that period: no foresight.
Setting parameters, such as share-weights, so the model reproduces observed base-year data.
The XML database GCAM writes its results to, read with queries.
